bug_description.normalized: The staged vulnerable source that matches the saved crash is the bundled libde265 checkout at commit ae638c6c2c08eccc0f973874d4f5175ec0cfcf6b, not the unrelated libheif metadata diff staged as `patch.diff`. In this checkout, the exact 499-byte HEIF witness is admitted by libheif, its embedded HEVC NAL units are passed into libde265, and `read_sao()` stores a band-mode `saoInfo` record into `ctb_info[].saoInfo` for the CTB later processed by the crashing worker, either directly from that CTB or by copying the left/up neighbor's already-stored record. `apply_sao_internal<unsigned short>` then reloads that persisted CTB state, rebuilds a 32-entry band table from `sao_band_position`, and indexes it as `bandTable[in_img[...] >> bandShift]` without clipping the input pixel to `maxPixelValue`. Because in-bounds bandTable entries can only be 0..4, the saved read at line 224 requires this lookup to read beyond `bandTable[31]`, yielding a stray positive `bandIdx` that is reused as `bandIdx-1` in `saoinfo->saoOffsetVal[cIdx][bandIdx-1]` and causes the observed 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow read. The saved ARVO metadata labels the sample as CWE-416 / heap-use-after-free, but the staged AddressSanitizer trace and upstream libde265 fix `ad291690a8c92218b9e86738edd45ed64736b246` both support this out-of-bounds-read root cause. Runtime disambiguation was disabled in `run_flags.json`, so Stage 02 does not claim which CTB supplied the merged `saoInfo` beyond the persisted `ctb_info[]` state that the worker actually reloads.

source.description: Reads the attacker-controlled HEVC SPS bit-depth fields from the coded bitstream. These fields later become `BitDepth_Y` or `BitDepth_C`, which make the crashing SAO channel high-bit-depth and determine `bandShift` for the vulnerable table lookup.
source.value_from: The exact staged witness `gt_results/arvo_18863/poc` is a 499-byte ISO Media / HEIC file with sha256 `f67663abd0d05925164d2422d32bb0d5731b765063d48f6dd8a0b87430891e81`. In the staged build, libheif's v1 libde265 wrapper (`LIBDE265_NUMERIC_VERSION 0x01000300`) splits the embedded HEVC payload into length-prefixed NAL units and feeds each raw NAL into libde265 via `de265_push_NAL`; these SPS fields are then decoded from that attacker-controlled bitstream.

sink.description: Uses the stray positive `bandIdx` from the bandTable over-read as `bandIdx-1` into the reloaded current-CTB `saoOffsetVal[cIdx]` array. That array has only four valid second-dimension indices (0..3), so this statement performs the saved 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow read.

root_cause.description: Indexes the 32-entry local `bandTable` with an unclipped decoded pixel value shifted by `bandShift`. On the saved path this happens in the reloaded CTB's band-mode `extendedTests` arm; because legal bandTable entries are only 0..4, a shifted pixel index above 31 is required to fabricate the later positive out-of-range `bandIdx`. Upstream fix `ad291690` clips the pixel to `maxPixelValue` before this lookup.

tainted_value_origin.note: In the sample metadata's vulnerable libheif commit `1fbc8b392526a00bbe18001a9731a61866949db6`, this guarded call forwards each attacker-controlled HEVC NAL payload into libde265. The prepared ARVO image carries the same container-to-codec handoff after later formatting churn, and the later SPS, slice, and SAO fields in the fine trace are decoded from these bytes.

parser_admitted.description: Once libheif has admitted the witness as a decodable HEIF image, the vulnerable libheif commit from sample metadata reaches this guarded `de265_push_NAL(...)` handoff for each length-prefixed HEVC NAL payload. The prepared ARVO image keeps the same handoff after later formatting churn, so the later SPS parsing, slice-header SAO parsing, and SAO worker crash all occur only after this container-to-codec transfer.

coarse_trace.summary: libheif accepts the crafted HEIF container, extracts its embedded HEVC NAL units, and hands them to libde265.
libde265 decodes the SPS bit-depth and global SAO-enable fields and persists them as `BitDepth_Y` and `BitDepth_C`.
Slice parsing enables SAO, and `read_sao()` either parses a supplier CTB's band-mode `saoInfo` or copies left/up neighbor state into the crashing CTB's persistent `ctb_info[].saoInfo` slot.

A SAO worker reloads the crashing CTB's persisted `saoInfo`, rebuilds the local band table from `sao_band_position`, over-reads that table with an unclipped pixel-derived index, and then reads past `saoOffsetVal` using the stray `bandIdx`.

fine_trace.note: Source. The attacker-controlled HEVC SPS materializes the luma and chroma bit-depth fields here. The crashing SAO channel later takes its `bitDepth` from one of these parsed values.
The SPS also turns SAO on globally. Without this bit, the slice header would not parse per-slice SAO flags and no CTB would enter `read_sao()` or the later SAO worker path.
Persists the parsed SPS bit-depth values into the stored SPS state. Later `img->get_bit_depth(cIdx)` and `apply_sao_internal()` read these exact `BitDepth_Y/C` fields on the crashing path.

Once SAO is globally enabled, the slice header parses per-slice SAO flags. `read_coding_tree_unit()` later calls `read_sao()` for a CTB only when `shdr->slice_sao_luma_flag || shdr->slice_sao_chroma_flag` is true.

When the current CTB has an available left neighbor in the same slice and tile, attacker bits decide whether this CTB inherits that neighbor's persistent SAO record. A set left-merge flag skips local SAO parsing for this CTB and makes the later left-neighbor copy into `ctb_info[xCtb,yCtb].saoInfo` possible.

If left-merge is not taken and an upper neighbor is available, attacker bits can instead make the current CTB inherit the upper neighbor's persistent SAO record. A set up-merge flag later copies `img->get_sao_info(xCtb,yCtb-1)` into the current CTB slot.

In whichever CTB actually supplies the crashing worker's `saoInfo` record, the non-merge arm decodes the per-channel SAO type into stack-local `saoinfo.SaoTypeIdx`. The later crash only fits band mode 1 for the crashing channel: type 0 returns at `sao.cc:40`, and type 2 takes the edge-offset branch at `sao.cc:78` instead of the vulnerable band-table path.

For that supplier CTB's band-mode channel, `read_sao()` decodes four offset magnitudes using the SPS-derived bit depth, applies the decoded signs, and stores the signed/scaled results in the four-entry `saoinfo.saoOffsetVal[cIdx]` array that the sink later indexes.
For the same supplier CTB in band mode, attacker bits choose `sao_band_position[cIdx]`. The worker later reloads this field as `saoLeftClass` to decide which four bandTable entries become nonzero.

The supplier CTB's stack-local `saoinfo` does not survive `read_sao()`. This store copies its parsed `SaoTypeIdx`, `sao_band_position`, and `saoOffsetVal` fields into persistent `ctb_info[].saoInfo` state. If the crashing CTB is itself non-merge, this is its own slot; otherwise this is the earlier store in the left/up supplier CTB that a later merge-copy reuses.

On the crashing CTB, a set merge flag overwrites its persistent `saoInfo` slot with the already-stored left or upper neighbor record. When both merge flags are zero this overwrite does not happen and the crashing slot remains the local store from step 10, but either way the worker later consumes only the persisted current-CTB slot. The saved artifacts do not disambiguate whether this overwrite happened for the crashing CTB.

The crashing SAO worker reloads the current CTB's persistent `saoInfo` from `ctb_info[]`. This closes the parser-to-worker state transfer: later `SaoTypeIdx`, `sao_band_position`, and `saoOffsetVal` uses all come from this reloaded CTB record, not from the earlier stack-local parse object.

The worker extracts the effective channel SAO type from the reloaded record. The saved crash only fits `SaoTypeIdx==1`: type 0 would return immediately at line 40, and type 2 would enter the edge-offset path at line 78 instead of the vulnerable band-mode table lookup.

Band mode derives the lookup shift from the SPS-persisted bit depth. The crashing frame is `apply_sao_internal<unsigned short>`, which already proves `img->high_bit_depth(cIdx)` was true; because step 18 executes the table lookup instead of the `bandShift >= 8` short-circuit, the effective crashing-channel bit depth is 9..12.
The worker reloads `sao_band_position` from the persisted current-CTB `saoInfo` and names it `saoLeftClass`. This field directly selects which four bandTable entries will become nonzero.

Using `saoLeftClass`, the worker zero-initializes the 32-entry local `bandTable` and assigns only four positions values 1..4. Any in-bounds lookup therefore returns only 0..4, and legal lookup indices are restricted to 0..31.

The saved sink line 224 is inside the `if (extendedTests)` arm at line 201, so the crashing CTB must have `has_pcm_or_cu_transquant_bypass` set. The staged artifacts do not disambiguate whether that CTB metadata came from PCM or transquant-bypass state.

Root cause. In the `extendedTests` band-mode arm, the code guards only on `bandShift` and indexes the 32-entry `bandTable` with `in_img[...] >> bandShift` without first clipping the decoded pixel to `maxPixelValue`. Because step 16 shows every legal bandTable entry is 0..4 yet step 19 requires a positive out-of-range `bandIdx`, the shifted pixel index must have exceeded 31 and this lookup must have read beyond `bandTable[31]`. Upstream fix `ad291690` inserts `pixel = Clip3(0,maxPixelValue,pixel)` before this lookup.

Sink. The stray positive `bandIdx` from step 18 passes `if (bandIdx>0)` and is reused as `bandIdx-1` into the four-entry `saoOffsetVal[cIdx]` array from the reloaded current-CTB `saoInfo`, so valid second-dimension indices are only 0..3. This is the exact 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow read reported by the saved AddressSanitizer trace at line 224 in `apply_sao_internal<unsigned short>`.

poc.trigger: Feed the exact staged 499-byte witness to libheif's `file-fuzzer`. libheif parses the HEIF container, forwards its embedded HEVC NAL units into libde265, and a SAO worker thread crashes while applying band-mode SAO to one CTB.

format.name: HEIF / ISO Media
format.contract: The only verified trigger is the exact staged 499-byte ISO Media / HEIC file `gt_results/arvo_18863/poc` with sha256 `f67663abd0d05925164d2422d32bb0d5731b765063d48f6dd8a0b87430891e81`. The saved artifacts prove only that this witness carries an HEVC image that libheif routes into libde265 and that one decoded CTB reaches high-bit-depth SAO band mode with `extendedTests` true and an out-of-range pixel value at the bandTable lookup; they do not disambiguate whether the crashing CTB used its own `saoInfo` or a left/up merged copy.
